survivingClaim: No statement about zeros of zeta. (a) HQ2(q, eps) has zeta's functional equation, integer frequencies, multiplicative coefficients a(n) >= 1, off-line zeros and order-4 poles on the line; its log-derivative coefficients are signed for every eps > 0 (first negative at k = 13, 22, 38, 67, 212, 669 for eps = 1e-1, 1e-2, 1e-3, 1e-4, 1e-6, 1e-8). (b) HQ3 and HQ4 have nu >= Lambda (HQ4 also a totally positive local sequence), off-line zeros and simple poles at real part 1/2 +- b; by Lemma N (Landau applied to one local factor) under nu >= 0 a real pole of the factor at real part >= that of every factor zero is unavoidable in the one-prime rational class. (c) For finitely many modified primes with rational local factors and zeta's functional equation: the multiplier splits into one-prime factors symmetric up to sign; a factor with no pole in |u| <= 1 is trivial; geometric local factors force G = zeta. These are elementary identification statements of known type, and within this class they select the same twins as the pole clause; the case of infinitely many modified primes is open. (d) On the band devices N(theta), W and C(theta) at heights 1e4 to 1e6, HQ2 enters only through Z_q - P_q; with factor zeros at distance <= 0.10 from the line it passes N(theta) at M = 1 in 384 of 384 object-cells with theta <= 0.85, and 801 certified pairs at M = 0 fail through the pole lattice alone; zeta is never certified negative. Device rows 10, 11, 12, 18 are ARGUED only. Verdict precise-obstruction stands.
obstruction: Screen complete, no device type. Coefficient-level reads (FE, integer frequencies, prime-power support, N >= 0) reject HQ2 only by the pole clause. Three reads reject HQ2 by another step: (a) sign of the log-derivative coefficients at powers of q, removed by the new siblings HQ3, HQ4 (nu >= Lambda, off-line zeros, simple poles at real part 1/2 +- b; Lemma N: under nu >= 0 a real pole right of the factor zeros is unavoidable in the one-prime rational class); (b) local Euler-factor shape at q; (c) complete multiplicativity at q. (b) and (c) are identifications: for finitely many modified primes with rational local factors and zeta's functional equation, geometric local factors force G = zeta (Lemmas S, F, C); within this class they select the same twins as the pole clause. Infinitely many modified primes: open. Band devices N(theta), W, C(theta) see HQ2 only through Z_q - P_q (distance of zeros and pole lattice). Rows 10, 11, 12, 18 (spinor S, D10 among them) are ARGUED, not run.

lesson: A one-prime twin with zeta's functional equation carries its off-line zeros and extra poles inside one local Euler factor, in Re s >= 1/2. Coefficient-level reads (FE, integer frequencies, prime-power support, N >= 0) meet only the pole clause; any read of local factor shape rejects the twin at that prime with no clause inside the strip; local positivity conditions do not (siblings HQ3, HQ4 with real poles right of the zeros pass them). Band devices order controls by distance of off-line zeros and by the pole lattice, not by multiplicativity. Compute note: repeated ball multiplication by a unit complex ball inflates radii about 1.4x per step; the first server unit was stopped and discarded for this.
followUp: Explore candidate for the planner: Euler-shape rigidity without the pole clause for infinitely many modified primes (first lemma: extend Lemma F to sets S with sum p^(-1/2) finite; kill test: a twin with geometric local factors and zeta's functional equation). It is an identification, usable as a pre-filter for local-shape devices, not a route to zeros. Also owed: a referee for Lemmas N, S, F, C and the device table; D10 Gram form and spinor S run on HQ2; engine control codes for HQ3 and HQ4 (MAP_ROW.md, lanes.jsonl in the lane directory).
